goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both point out that using `indexOf` for origin validation is unsafe because it performs substring/prefix matching instead of an exact origin comparison, allowing malicious lookalike domains to bypass the check (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`).

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both point to the same core problem: `postMessage` is using `request.referer` as `targetOrigin`, which is not a reliable/valid targetOrigin value. The candidate emphasizes cases where the referrer is missing/stripped (causing errors), while the golden emphasizes that using a full URL (not just origin) will cause messages to be dropped. These are closely related consequences of the same incorrect use of `request.referer` for targetOrigin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Attacker-chosen embed_url is interpolated unescaped into an href attribute of a raw_html post, so a URL like https://host/p?x'onmouseover='alert(1) injects stored XSS.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the attacker-influenced `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML anchor with single-quoted attributes: `"#{url}"` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or event-handler injection. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` unescaped and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so a crafted URL containing `'` can break out of the href attribute and produce stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — raw_html cook_method bypasses all sanitization, so feed/readability HTML (javascript: hrefs, arbitrary tags from RSS) is rendered via `raw post.cooked`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook` early-returning `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where sanitization would typically occur). Feed import (`Jobs::PollFeed`) passes `i.content` from RSS/ATOM into `TopicEmbed.import` and creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html`, and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Neither the RSS path nor `TopicEmbed.import_remote`’s readability filtering shows any explicit sanitization or scheme filtering (e.g., `javascript:` in `href/src`), so untrusted HTML can be stored and rendered as-is, enabling XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — Throttle is keyed on the exact URL string, so varying query strings on the embeddable host lets anyone with a spoofed Referer force unlimited remote fetches and topic creation.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? uses a Redis key derived from the full embed URL string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so changing the query string changes the throttle key and bypasses the 60s throttle. Additionally, perform_retrieve checks existing embeds by exact `embed_url` (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`), and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`import` store the exact URL as `embed_url` with a unique index, so varying query strings will result in new TopicEmbed rows and new topics/posts. Since EmbedController only validates the Referer host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, a client that can supply/forge a matching Referer can repeatedly trigger remote fetch + topic creation by varying the URL string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:17 — Every cache miss enqueues a retrieve job with only a client-controlled Referer check, and no dedupe of pending jobs, enabling job-queue flooding.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (no check for an already-enqueued/pending job). The only request gate shown is `ensure_embeddable`, which relies on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`—a client-supplied header. Since `embed_url` is also client-controlled and can be varied per request, an attacker who can satisfy/spoof the Referer can trigger many enqueues and downstream fetches (via `TopicRetriever`/`open(url)`), creating a queue-flood/DoS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Each retrieve synchronously re-runs the whole PollFeed, so N unique embed URLs amplify into N full feed fetches and imports.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve: when SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? is true, it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline for every retrieve attempt before falling back to HTTP fetch. The throttle in `retrieved_recently?` is per-embed URL key (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so N distinct embed URLs can each trigger a full feed fetch/parse/import loop in Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` then `rss.items.each ... TopicEmbed.import`). This is a scalability/performance/architecture issue rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — Any item raising (e.g. nil content on RSS items using description, or an import error) aborts the loop with retry:false, silently skipping all remaining items.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — Check-then-create on embed_url races between concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic (staff bypasses throttle), causing RecordNotUnique job failures after PostCreator side effects.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!` inside the “no embed” branch, while the migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. With concurrent callers (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` iterating RSS items and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` fetching the same `embed_url`, and `RetrieveTopic` can disable throttling for staff via `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`), two processes can both see no row and then one will raise `RecordNotUnique` on `create!`. There’s no rescue/retry logic in `import`, so this can surface as job failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 — Kernel#open on the feed_polling_url setting allows a "|cmd" value to execute shell commands (admin-to-RCE) and follows redirects without restriction.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. Using `Kernel#open` with `open-uri` on a setting-controlled string can treat inputs like `"|cmd"` as a shell pipeline (via `IO.popen`) and will also follow HTTP redirects by default; the diff adds this unsafe `open(...)` usage without validation or restrictions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — content_sha1 is updated even when revise! returns false or save fails, silently marking stale content as synced forever.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb, around the `else` block). The diff shows `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` early (`return false if not should_revise?`), and `update_post` now does `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` without checking the return value. Therefore the embed row can be marked with the new `content_sha1` even if the post wasn’t actually revised/saved, potentially preventing future updates because the SHA1 no longer indicates “changed”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin check uses substring indexOf, so a prefix origin (e.g. https://forum.example.co) passes the postMessage validation.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — The `--category` option was removed from the disqus import CLI and `created_at` was dropped, so existing invocations using `-c` break and imported topics lose their original dates.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Disqus Thor CLI `--category` option (deleted `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'`) and also replaces the `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` call with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not pass `created_at` or any category. As a result, existing `disqus:import` invocations using `-c/--category` will fail option parsing, and imported topics/posts will no longer preserve the original `created_at` from the Disqus thread data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — The postMessage targetOrigin is the raw `request.referer`, so when the referer is missing or stripped (e.g. by a Referrer-Policy) postMessage throws and the documented discourse-resize contract fails silently.
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core problem: `postMessage` is using `request.referer` as `targetOrigin`, which is not a reliable/valid targetOrigin value. The candidate emphasizes cases where the referrer is missing/stripped (causing errors), while the golden emphasizes that using a full URL (not just origin) will cause messages to be dropped. These are closely related consequences of the same incorrect use of `request.referer` for targetOrigin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — The embed snippet only works if the undocumented `discourseUrl` global ends with a trailing slash, otherwise it builds a broken `...comembed/best` URL.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the iframe URL is built via simple string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. If `discourseUrl` does not end with `/`, the resulting URL becomes `...comembed/best` (missing slash) and will be broken. The diff does not show any normalization ensuring a trailing slash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — The origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` is a substring match rather than an exact origin comparison, which makes the resize-message contract accept prefix-matching origins.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using `indexOf` for origin validation is unsafe because it performs substring/prefix matching instead of an exact origin comparison, allowing malicious lookalike domains to bypass the check (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:27 — The new `embeddable_host` setting is matched exactly against the referer host, so an embedding site served on both www/non-www or a non-default port is rejected and the setting takes only a single host.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, embedding is allowed only when `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which is an exact host match and therefore will reject a different subdomain such as `www.example.com` vs `example.com` unless the setting is changed. However, the finding’s mention of “non-default port” is not supported by the diff because `URI(...).host` ignores the port (it would still be `example.com`). This is a real limitation/edge-case of the new setting, but not necessarily a defect given the setting is explicitly a single “Host that can embed…”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — Protocol-relative URLs ("//cdn/x") match start_with?('/') and are rewritten to "http://host/cdn/x", breaking links/images.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both the and rewrites check `href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')` and then strip all leading slashes via `sub(/^\/+/, '')` before prefixing with `#{scheme}://#{host}`. This will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x`, rewriting them to `http(s):///cdn.example.com/x`, which breaks such links/images. The finding correctly points to this behavior in the added method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post can be nil (post deleted/destroyed) and is passed to PostRevisor, raising NoMethodError on revise.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then, if the content SHA changes, immediately does `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)` without guarding against `post` being nil. Because `topic_embeds` only stores `post_id` and `belongs_to :post` will return nil if the referenced Post has been deleted/destroyed, this can raise (e.g., NoMethodError inside PostRevisor when it expects a Post). The diff does not add any validation on `post_id` existence or nil handling in this branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21 — Check-then-create race: concurrent imports of same URL both see blank embed, create duplicate topics and the loser hits a unique-index exception.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank creates a new topic/post and then `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`. With concurrent imports of the same `url`, both can observe `embed.blank?` and create separate topics/posts; when both reach `create!`, one will hit the unique index and raise, leaving an extra topic/post created by the losing transaction attempt (or at least causing an exception). No locking or rescue/retry is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content is nil for RSS items that only have description, so .scrub raises and aborts the whole feed poll.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `i.content` can be nil for RSS items that only provide `description`, causing `.scrub` to raise and break polling—this is the same nil/absent `content` issue described in the golden comment (which also suggests falling back to `description`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Non-atomic setnx then expire: if the process dies between them the key never expires and the URL is throttled forever.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is set with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then expiration is applied in a separate call `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic; if the process crashes or the Redis connection drops after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key can remain without a TTL, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true indefinitely and permanently throttling that `@embed_url`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — Port omission ignores scheme, so https on port 80 or http on port 443 produces a prefix without the required port.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix-building logic appends the port only when `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This treats 80 and 443 as universally “default” and omits them regardless of scheme. For URLs like `https://example.com:80/...` or `http://example.com:443/...`, `uri.port` will be 80/443 respectively, the condition will be false, and the resulting `prefix` will incorrectly drop the explicit port, producing wrong absolutized links.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — contents << mutates the caller's string (and raises on frozen strings) instead of building a new string.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends in-place to the passed-in `contents` string, which can unintentionally mutate the caller’s object. This is verifiable in the diff. While it can raise if a frozen string is passed, the diff does not show any caller providing a frozen string or reusing `contents` later, so it’s a real design/edge-case concern rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — "end if" modifier makes the next ERB output statement the if-condition, working only by accident since the logo append is truthy.
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: using `end if` to close an ERB/Ruby `if` block is incorrect/unsafe and can break rendering; it should be a plain `end`. The candidate explains the misparse/accidental behavior caused by the `if` modifier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Already-shipped migration edited to add `force: true`, which silently drops and recreates top_topics (losing data) if re-run, and diverges from deployed history.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists and recreates it, which can cause silent data loss if this migration is re-run (e.g., via rollback/redo or in certain deploy/reset scenarios) and also changes historical migration behavior compared to environments that already ran the prior version.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — create_table ... force: true` silently drops any existing topic_embeds table instead of failing, a destructive DDL with no rollback of data.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` explicitly uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which (in Rails) will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. While this is a new migration so the table normally won’t exist in a typical forward migration path, the review concern is real and diff-grounded: `force: true` is an unnecessarily destructive option that could cause data loss if the migration is reapplied/loaded in an environment where `topic_embeds` already exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adding NOT NULL column with default to the large posts table rewrites the whole table under an exclusive lock on pre-11 Postgres, with no batched backfill.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb). On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a NOT NULL column with a non-null DEFAULT generally forces a full table rewrite and takes an exclusive lock for the duration. This is a deployment/operational risk for a potentially large `posts` table, but not an application correctness defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — Removing the --category option and switching the importer to TopicEmbed.import_remote is an unrelated behavior change bundled into the embed PR, and it silently drops category support.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor explicitly removes the `method_option :category` and deletes the code that resolves `category_id` from `options[:category]`. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which provides no category selection path. This is a real, diff-grounded scope/backwards-compatibility behavior change (dropping a CLI option and its functionality) bundled into an embed-related PR, but it’s not necessarily a correctness defect in the embed feature itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — TopicRetriever calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute directly, which ties a lib class to a scheduled job's internals instead of a shared feed-import service.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, the lib class directly instantiates and runs a scheduled job: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. This creates tight coupling between a core retrieval service (`TopicRetriever`) and a scheduled job’s implementation details rather than delegating to a shared feed-import/polling service layer. It’s an architecture/design concern grounded in the diff, not an immediate correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 — The embed_by_username user lookup is copied from app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:25 and should live in a single helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated logic for resolving the embedding user by username: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` repeats the same lookup. This is a maintainability/architecture concern (DRY), not a functional defect, and it is grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:62 — The a[href] and img[src] absolutizing loops at lines 62 and 68 are near-identical copies and could be one parameterized loop.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, there are indeed two similar loops (one for fragment.css('a') updating href, one for fragment.css('img') updating src), but this is a DRY/refactor suggestion rather than a defect or substantive review issue. The behavior is clear and correct as written; the finding amounts to a style/duplication nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — import appends to the caller's contents string in place with <<, a hidden side effect that leaks across the method boundary.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the method mutates its `contents` argument in place via `contents << "\n<hr>..."` before computing `content_sha1` and creating/updating posts. This is a real, diff-grounded side effect that can leak back to callers if they reuse the same String instance, but the diff does not show an immediate correctness failure from this behavior (it’s primarily an encapsulation/maintainability concern).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — The unused require_dependency 'email/sender' is dead code, probably copied from another job.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is present at the top but nothing in this file references `Email::Sender` (the job only looks up a user and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`). This makes the require look unnecessary in this context, though the diff alone can’t prove it has no intentional side effects elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Adding force: true to an existing unrelated migration, plus whitespace-only edits in 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb, is an unrelated change bundled in.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes unrelated changes outside the embedding/feed feature: it modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (previously without `force`), and makes whitespace-only/newline edits in `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` (trailing whitespace removal and adding a missing newline). These are scope/bundling issues and alter historical migrations without being tied to the feature being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:37 — The embed.permalink translation key is added but never referenced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `embed.permalink` under `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and the added/modified code in this PR only references other `embed.*` keys (`title`, `start_discussion`, `continue`, `loading`, `imported_from`) in `app/views/embed/*` and `TopicEmbed.import`. No reference to `embed.permalink` is shown, so it appears unused, but that’s a minor unused-translation nit rather than a verifiable defect or substantial review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:42 — On every embed cache miss the retriever synchronously re-runs the entire PollFeed job (fetch full feed and import/SHA/Nokogiri every item), and the throttle is keyed per embed_url so distinct URLs each trigger a full feed poll.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve synchronously calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to HTTP fetch. This happens on an embed cache miss (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` is false). Separately, the throttle key in `retrieved_recently?` is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, so requests for many distinct embed URLs can each bypass the throttle and trigger a full feed poll. This is a concrete performance/architecture issue grounded in the diff, but not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16 — Every uncached embed request (and each 30s loading-page reload per viewer) enqueues a new retrieve_topic job with no enqueue-side dedupe, flooding Sidekiq for popular pages.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) is nil it unconditionally calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... , embed_url: embed_url) on every request, and the loading page reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) causing repeated requests. The only throttling/dedupe shown is inside TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (Redis) which prevents repeated fetching but does not prevent enqueuing many Sidekiq jobs, so popular uncached embeds can flood the queue until the embed exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote does open(url).read with no timeout or size cap, materializing arbitrarily large remote bodies in memory before Readability parsing.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote (new in this diff), it does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`, which fetches the entire remote response body into memory with no explicit timeout, read timeout, or maximum size guard. This can allow slow/large responses to tie up workers and potentially cause memory/availability issues (DoS) before parsing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 — Feed is fetched via open() with no timeout/size limit and every item is re-imported (string build, SHA1, DB lookup) each poll with no Last-Modified/ETag check despite defining feed_key.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed is fetched with `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and no explicit timeout/size limit is set in this diff. The job then iterates `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for each item every poll; although `TopicEmbed.import` avoids recreating unchanged posts via `content_sha1`/DB lookup, it still performs per-item SHA1 computation and DB queries each run. A `feed_key` method is defined but never used, and there is no Last-Modified/ETag conditional fetch logic shown. This is a concrete robustness/performance concern grounded in the diff, but not a directly verifiable functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote fetches an arbitrary remote URL via open-uri with no open/read timeout, so a slow host can hang the Sidekiq worker indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote, the code does `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` or other bounding. This method is invoked from background execution paths (e.g., TopicRetriever#fetch_http and Jobs::RetrieveTopic), so a slow or non-responsive remote host can block the Sidekiq worker thread/process for an unbounded time, causing availability issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Feed polling does outbound HTTP via open() with no timeout and no error handling, so a hung or failing feed stalls or kills the job (retry: false).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job performs outbound HTTP with `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (line ~29) using `open-uri` without specifying `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` and without any `rescue` around network/parse failures. Since this is a scheduled Sidekiq job with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a hung connection can stall the worker thread, and common network errors (timeouts, DNS, invalid RSS) can cause the job to fail with no retry—both are real runtime failure modes introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — An item with nil content (or any single import error) raises and aborts processing of all remaining feed items since there is no per-item rescue.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` for each `rss.items` entry with no per-item error handling. If `i.content` is `nil` (or any item has malformed data causing an exception), calling `.scrub` (and/or `CGI.unescapeHTML`) will raise and abort the entire job, preventing remaining feed items from being processed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Non-atomic setnx followed by expire can leave a throttle key with no TTL if the process dies in between, permanently blocking retrieval of that URL.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle is implemented as `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands; if the process crashes or is interrupted after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be created without a TTL and `retrieved_recently?` will return true forever for that embed URL, permanently throttling retrieval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Each retrieve job synchronously runs the entire PollFeed (full feed download and import) for one URL, amplifying load and overlapping with the hourly job.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http`. Since TopicRetriever is invoked by the regular job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (triggered when an embed is requested and no TopicEmbed exists), each retrieve can synchronously trigger a full feed poll/import (see app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb uses `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and iterates all items). This is a concrete load/architecture concern and can overlap with the hourly scheduled PollFeed job, even though it may not be a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — topic_embed.rb uses open() on a URL without requiring open-uri itself, relying on poll_feed.rb being loaded first (e.g. in the disqus thor task it may treat the URL as a file path).

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb, `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but the file does not `require 'open-uri'`. Only Jobs::PollFeed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) requires `open-uri`, so callers like lib/tasks/disqus.thor (now using `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) could invoke `open()` without URI support loaded, causing `open("http://...")` to be treated like a local file path and fail (e.g., ENOENT).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — Check-then-create on embed_url races between concurrent retrieve jobs (staff are unthrottled), so the unique index raises RecordNotUnique and the job fails.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` when `embed.blank?`. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so concurrent jobs importing the same URL can both see no row and then race on `create!`, causing one to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and fail (no rescue/retry shown). This is made more likely because `TopicRetriever` throttling can be disabled via `no_throttle` for staff (`TopicRetriever.new(..., no_throttle: user.try(:staff?))`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — Loading page reloads every 30s forever with no retry cap, and each reload enqueues another retrieve job even when retrieval permanently fails.

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, then renders `embed/loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:11-18). The loading template unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-11). If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., permanent fetch/parse failure), the page will reload indefinitely and each request will enqueue another `:retrieve_topic` job, since there is no retry cap or backoff in the view/controller logic. Although `TopicRetriever` throttles actual retrieval to once per 60s, the repeated enqueuing/requests still happens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — raw_html cook_method returns imported RSS/remote HTML unsanitized, and best.html.erb renders it with `raw`, so a feed or remote page can plant stored XSS (scripts, javascript: hrefs)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post#cook` early-returning `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` using RSS/remote HTML content (`PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `Readability::Document` allowing `a/img` with `href/src`). There is no sanitization step in `TopicEmbed.import`/`absolutize_urls`, and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). This makes stored XSS via feed/remote content (e.g., `javascript:` URLs or other unsafe attributes/markup) a real risk grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Feed-supplied url goes into the imported_from anchor `href='#{url}'` without escaping, so a quote in the URL enables attribute/HTML injection

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `contents << "...#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}` interpolates `url` directly into a single-quoted `href` attribute. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the attribute. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and later rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, this enables HTML/attribute injection (XSS) from feed-supplied URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16 — Anonymous requests can queue retrieve_topic for any distinct URL on the embeddable host, and the 60s throttle is keyed per URL, so topic-creation spam is unbounded

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` even for `current_user == nil` (anonymous). The job calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, whose only throttle (`retrieved_recently?`) is keyed by `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (per-URL) with a 60s TTL, not per client/IP/user. Since `invalid_host?` only restricts the URL host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, an attacker (or any visitor from the embeddable host, and even a forged Referer header given `ensure_embeddable` relies on `request.referer`) can trigger retrieval for arbitrarily many distinct URLs on that host, causing unbounded topic creation/fetching work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Kernel#open(url) via open-uri follows redirects off the embeddable host (SSRF), and the Disqus importer passes unvalidated links to it, where a leading pipe runs a command

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). This uses `Kernel#open` on an untrusted string and does not require/perform any allowlisting of scheme/host for `url` in this method. In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the importer now passes `t[:link]` directly into `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (replacing the prior behavior of just embedding the permalink), so a malicious or unexpected link could be fetched. `open-uri`/`open` will follow HTTP redirects, so even if the initial host were acceptable elsewhere, the final request could redirect off-host (SSRF). Additionally, `Kernel#open` historically treats strings beginning with `|` as a command to execute, so passing an unvalidated `t[:link]` could lead to command execution in affected Ruby configurations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:27 — Referer-based host check is the only embed gate and can be spoofed or stripped, and X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is not a valid value
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core security concerns: using Referer-based validation as the primary gate (spoofable/strippable) and setting X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL, which undermines framing/clickjacking protections. It doesn’t explicitly mention the nil-to-empty-string fallback masking failures, but overall it targets the same underlying issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — postMessage origin check uses substring indexOf, so a prefix-matching origin like https://forum.example.co passes

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler checks `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This treats any `e.origin` that is a substring/prefix of `discourseUrl` as trusted. For example, if `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.example.com/`, an attacker origin like `https://forum.example.co` would make `indexOf` return 0 and bypass the check, allowing untrusted postMessages to trigger iframe resizing. This is a verifiable security defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:20 — discourse_expires_in caches the TopicView rendered for current_user, which may expose user-specific content through shared caches

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the rendered content is based on `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`, which can vary by `current_user` (e.g., permissions/visibility). The action then unconditionally calls `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`, potentially marking the response cacheable. The diff does not show whether `discourse_expires_in` varies cache keys/headers by user (e.g., `Vary: Cookie`) or forces private caching, so an actual leak via shared caches can’t be verified from the diff alone, but the concern is specific and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41 — Test expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve directly but controller only calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic), so the spec depends on synchronous job execution and never asserts the enqueue itself.

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best, when no topic_id is found the controller enqueues a job: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`; it never calls `TopicRetriever` directly. However, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve` to be invoked in that branch, so the spec is incorrect and would fail against the controller behavior (it also doesn’t assert the enqueue).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:25 — No test for a referer whose host differs from embeddable_host or a malformed referer, which is the core validation added in ensure_embeddable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds core validation in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` that rejects requests when `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` to raise invalid access. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, tests cover missing `embed_url`, missing `embeddable_host`, and the case with no referer, plus a success case where referer == embed_url. There is no test exercising (1) a referer present but with a different host than `embeddable_host`, or (2) a malformed referer that triggers the `URI::InvalidURIError` rescue path. This is a specific missing-test issue for newly added nontrivial logic, not a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32 — retrieved_recently? is stubbed in every case, so the redis setnx/expire throttle and the no_throttle staff bypass have no real coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the two “valid host” examples both stub `retrieved_recently?` (`returns(false)` and `returns(true)`), so the actual throttle implementation in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (the `$redis.setnx`/`expire` logic) is never exercised. The early bypass `return false if @opts[:no_throttle]` is also not covered by any spec (no test constructs `TopicRetriever.new(embed_url, no_throttle: true)`), even though that path is used by Jobs::RetrieveTopic (`no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`). This is a specific missing-test gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a functional defect in the implementation itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:27 — perform_retrieve is always mocked; the existing-embed short-circuit, RSS-first fallback, and fetch_http/missing-user paths are untested.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb the tests stub/expect `perform_retrieve` (e.g., `topic_retriever.expects(:perform_retrieve).once/never`) and also stub `retrieved_recently?`, so none of the actual logic inside `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` is exercised. The new method contains nontrivial control flow (short-circuit if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, RSS-first fallback via `Jobs::PollFeed` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?`, and `fetch_http` which returns early if the `embed_by_username` user is missing before calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). Those paths are indeed untested by the current spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — The "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" tests pass vacuously because feed_polling_enabled defaults to false, so they do not isolate the condition they name.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed runs only if all three conditions are true: feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the “requires feed_polling_url” test only stubs feed_polling_url to nil (and does not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true nor embed_by_username to present), and the “requires embed_by_username” test only stubs embed_by_username to nil. Given the defaults added in config/site_settings.yml (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: '', embed_by_username: ''), these tests can pass without isolating the named condition because the guard can already fail on feed_polling_enabled?/blank defaults.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:31 — poll_feed is only mocked; the feed parsing, link/id fallback, missing-user return, and TopicEmbed.import calls are never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: The spec at spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only asserts the guard conditions in execute and that poll_feed is called (mocked) when settings are present. It never exercises Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed itself (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), including SimpleRSS parsing, the link/id fallback logic, the early return when the user lookup fails, or the loop calling TopicEmbed.import. This is a concrete test gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — The new RetrieveTopic job (missing embed_url raise, staff no_throttle mapping) has no spec.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` with nontrivial behavior (raises `Discourse::InvalidParameters` when `args[:embed_url]` is missing, looks up optional `user_id`, and passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever`). There is no corresponding spec file covering this job (unlike `TopicRetriever`, `PollFeed`, etc.). However, the finding’s parenthetical is incorrect: the job *does* include the missing-`embed_url` raise and the staff `no_throttle` mapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40 — The update test only checks the content changed; it does not cover the unchanged-sha1 no-revise path, the content_sha1 update, or that no second topic/embed was created.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb the “Supports updating the post” example only asserts that calling TopicEmbed.import again with the same URL and different contents results in updated cooked text. It does not exercise the branch in TopicEmbed.import where content_sha1 is unchanged (so no revise occurs), nor does it assert that embed.content_sha1 is updated via embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) when content changes, or that the second import does not create an additional TopicEmbed/topic (creation happens only when embed.blank?). These are specific, diff-grounded coverage gaps in newly added nontrivial logic, not an app defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:34 — absolutize_urls edge cases are untested: protocol-relative "//host" URLs, which get rewritten incorrectly, non-default ports, and https URLs.

adjudication.rationale: TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls rewrites any href/src starting with '/' (TopicEmbed#absolutize_urls). That includes protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/x", which will be incorrectly rewritten to "#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x" because it strips leading slashes and prepends the source site prefix. The current spec only covers simple root-relative "/path" cases and does not cover this failing behavior (nor https/non-default ports).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — The new skip_validations behavior in PostRevisor#revise_post has no direct test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post to conditionally skip validations via `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. While `TopicEmbed.import` calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)` and the `topic_embed_spec` exercises an update path, no spec explicitly verifies the new behavior (i.e., that validations are actually bypassed when `skip_validations` is set, or that a revision would succeed when it would otherwise fail validation). This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage concern rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:18 — Only non-http URL rejection is tested; import_remote, which fetches and runs Readability, has no coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial behavior in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (fetching remote content via `open(url).read` and extracting `doc.title`/`doc.content` using `Readability::Document`), but the added spec `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only exercises `.import` (including malformed URL rejection) and does not cover `.import_remote` at all. This is a specific, diff-grounded testing gap for newly introduced logic rather than a verified functional defect.
